content: Neonatal sepsis and necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) are significant causes of mortality and morbidity in newborns, even when appropriate antibiotic therapy is administered. Lactoferrin, a naturally occurring glycoprotein with antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties, has been proposed as a potential adjunct to antibiotics to enhance host defense mechanisms and modulate inflammation in these conditions. The hypothesis is that the addition of lactoferrin to standard antibiotic therapy might improve clinical outcomes in neonates with sepsis, NEC, or both. The primary aim of this review was to evaluate the safety and efficacy of oral lactoferrin as an adjunctive treatment to antibiotics in neonates with suspected or confirmed sepsis, NEC, or both. To achieve this, a comprehensive search was conducted using the Cochrane Neonatal standard search strategy. Databases searched included the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), MEDLINE via PubMed, PREMEDLINE, Embase, and CINAHL, covering studies published up to September 20, 2018. Additional sources such as clinical trial registries, conference proceedings, reference lists of retrieved articles, and personal files of the authors were also reviewed. The inclusion criteria for this review were randomized or quasi-randomized controlled trials that evaluated enteral lactoferrin, at any dose or duration, as an adjunct to antibiotic therapy. Comparisons were made with antibiotic therapy alone (with or without placebo) or other adjunctive treatments. The population of interest included neonates of any gestational age up to 44 weeks' postmenstrual age with confirmed or suspected sepsis or NEC (Bell's Stage II or III). The methodological quality of the studies was assessed using standardized Cochrane Neonatal methods. Titles and abstracts identified through the search were independently reviewed by two authors, and full-text articles were obtained when necessary. Data extraction and trial inclusion/exclusion were recorded using pre-designed forms. The quality of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE approach. The review did not identify any eligible trials that evaluated the use of lactoferrin for the treatment of neonatal sepsis or NEC. As a result, no conclusions could be drawn regarding the safety or efficacy of enteral lactoferrin as an adjunct to antibiotics in these conditions. The authors concluded that, at present, there is no evidence to support or refute the use of enteral lactoferrin as an adjunctive therapy for neonatal sepsis or NEC. Furthermore, given the lack of evidence supporting the efficacy of enteral lactoferrin in preventing late-onset sepsis and NEC, further research into its use as an adjunctive treatment for these conditions does not appear to be a priority.
